failure_summary.description: Returned a named example instead of the role it exemplified.
Overlooked the exact clue meaning, requested answer slot, or identifying relation despite existing guidance.
Used a noncanonical expanded name or singular form where the expected answer was abbreviated or plural.
The current-king wording supports Abdullah II, while the expected answer relies on historical context about Hussein.

patch.reasoning: Most errors are already covered by the skill’s exact-meaning, slot, and answer-form rules, so repeating those instructions is unlikely to help. One targeted clarification can prevent a named exemplar from being mistaken for the requested role.

edits.target: - In trivia or wordplay clues, treat a parenthetical number as a hard answer-length constraint. For a double-definition clue (for example, “X, or what Y is put to”), seek the exact word that fits both senses rather than a synonym that fits only one. Use any proper-name cue to identify the requested name or name part.
edits.content: - In trivia or wordplay clues, treat a parenthetical number as a hard answer-length constraint. For a double-definition clue (for example, “X, or what Y is put to”), seek the exact word that fits both senses rather than a synonym that fits only one. Use a proper-name cue to identify a name only when the requested slot is a name or name part. If a name is introduced as an example (“like X”) to signal a shared role or category, return that role or category, not the example’s name.
